text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Drug approval process criticized: Some Health Canada managers passed products despite reviewers' concerns, insiders say.
- Hospital put hush on death, court told: Probe impeded, affidavit states.
- Yeltsin startles NATO leaders: President gets 'carried away' with remarks on removing nuclear warheads.
- Congo ban on political parties wins praise: First things first, African leaders say.
- B.C. warned against Reform: Don't contribute to national unity problem, Chretien says.
- Sperm donor granted access to son: Fathers 'integral part' of child's life, Alberta judge rules in 'novel' sperm-pact case.
- Bid launched for Coke bottler: Coca-Cola Enterprises offers C$747-million for Canadian counterpart as stock bubbles up.
- Bank of Montreal profit rolls along in 2nd quarter: Nesbitt's Bre-X hit just C$5-million; Scotiabank reports record earnings.
- Conrad Black mulls national paper: Expects Hollinger to make decision some time this year.
- Legal woes may be brewing for Molson: Part-owner Miller could have claims.
- C$743-million bid for Coke Canada: Giant U.S. bottler makes cash offer for its Canadian counterpart as Coca-Cola attempts to streamline its bottling operations.
- Bonds and C$ hit by pre-election jitters.
